note: WIDE design funnel, restricted to keywords_design.json category allowed_domains. METHOD: publisher RSS/Atom sweeps + dev.to API + direct og/JSON-LD parsing; every published_iso came from article:published_time, JSON-LD datePublished, or publisher feed pubDate, then gated with pipeline/freshness.py (72h, cutoff 2026-08-05T22:00:26Z). ACCESS NOTES: eleken.co RSS dates are UPDATED dates - all five 'fresh-looking' Eleken posts (Generative UI, Vibe Design, AI Prototyping, Multimodal UX, Design Systems) actually carry July published dates in their page markup and were DROPPED as stale; parallelhq.com is programmatic 'Best X Agencies in <city>' SEO spam and was skipped entirely; 80.lv had zero fresh AI/design items (its Octane story is Dec 2025); keyshot.com, mindstudio.ai, palettt.com, orq.ai, sgwdesignworks.com, boston-engineering.com, getleo.ai and builder.io return 404/empty feeds; all3dp.com and fastcompany.com return 403 to direct fetch (Fast Company reached via /technology/rss); figma.com/blog has nothing newer than 2026-08-05T18:16 (already published), and the 08-05 release note (AI credit limits) falls outside the window, so Figma is represented via its YouTube channel; instagram.com skipped per run instruction. YouTube upload times verified via channel Atom feeds (videos.xml). Already-published design stories excluded: Vercel Agent Plugins 1.0.0/v0 API/eve browser, Claude-to-Figma + Claude screen states, Eleken Figma-to-Claude-Code, Armature rigging, Cascadeur 2026.2, Material Creator, Creo AI, Backflip AI, Designesy 40-check scoring, Road to VR Electronauts, State of CSS 2026, Figma Code Connect MCP. Dropped for the design-relevance test: VentureBeat agent-orchestration/security pieces, CIO enterprise-AI governance, engineering.com M&A items, css-tricks Dialog element (no AI hook), UploadVR game reviews, NVIDIA open-world-models post (already used by another section - cross-section collision risk). Per-source cap of 3 enforced: dev.to 3, creativebloq 3, vercel 3, uxdesign 3, youtube 3, roadtovr 2, engineering.com 2, and one each from cgchannel, engadget, fastcompany, venturebeat, logrocket - 12 distinct outlets.

items.excerpt: Agent-built interfaces default to lifeless boxes because nothing in the loop enforces craft. The author wires a 'UI/UX Excellence Prover' MCP into the agent so spring physics, eight interaction states per component, and spatial hierarchy become checkable requirements instead of taste.
items.title: Your AI agent's UI is mediocre—and here's how to fix it

items.excerpt: A practical account of feeding an AI coding agent explicit design taste — type scale, spacing rhythm, restraint rules — instead of hoping the model guesses. The argument is that 'taste' is transferable if you write it down as constraints the agent can be judged against.
items.title: Teaching Your AI Web Design Some Actual Taste

items.excerpt: Tired of manually reading DevTools to reconstruct another site's type ramp, palette and spacing scale, the author shipped a Chrome extension that extracts a live page's design tokens automatically. It turns competitive teardown into a one-click token dump.
items.title: I got tired of reverse-engineering design systems by hand, so I built a Chrome extension

items.excerpt: Chat SDK's requestApproval pauses a running agent workflow, posts an Approve/Deny card into the conversation, and resumes when a human decides — even across a server restart. Human-in-the-loop approval becomes a durable UI primitive rather than a modal you have to babysit.
items.title: Pause workflows for approval with Chat SDK

items.excerpt: skills.sh now lets you bundle multiple agent skills into a single shareable pack that installs and updates with one command. For a design org this is the distribution channel for house style, component rules and review checklists across every teammate's agent.
items.title: Skill packs are now available on skills.sh

items.excerpt: ByteDance's Seedance 2.5 lands on Vercel AI Gateway with up to 30-second single clips, multimodal reference input, targeted editing, and asynchronous generation that survives a dropped session. Long-form generative video becomes an API call inside an ordinary product stack.
items.title: Seedance 2.5 now available on Vercel AI Gateway

items.excerpt: Runway adds Seedance 2.5 to its platform, putting ByteDance's long-clip video model directly next to Runway's own generation and editing tools. Runway keeps positioning itself as the multi-model workbench rather than a single-model studio.
items.title: Seedance 2.5 is Now Available on Runway

items.excerpt: Adobe demos taking an idea to finished content through a single chat thread rather than hopping between apps and panels. The pitch is conversational orchestration across Creative Cloud, with Firefly doing the generation underneath.
items.title: Turn your ideas into finished content with one chat

items.excerpt: Figma walks through the engineering behind making copy and paste dramatically faster — the least glamorous interaction in the tool and one of the most used. A reminder that perceived craft in a design tool is mostly latency work nobody announces.
items.title: How Figma made copy + paste faster

items.excerpt: Photoshop 27.9.1 moves the Remove tool into the contextual task bar, adds inline prompt tips to Generate Image, and lets you push multiple layers straight to Firefly Boards. Small release, but it shows the AI tools migrating into the default toolbar path.
items.title: Adobe releases Photoshop 27.9.1

items.excerpt: Ed Catmull, who co-founded Pixar and helped invent modern CG animation, has joined the jury of Higgsfield's $1m generative-AI film festival. The animation community's reaction says a lot about who gets to legitimise AI filmmaking.
items.title: Pixar co-founder's new AI role is reigniting animation's biggest debate

items.excerpt: DuckDuckGo's sold-out 'Normal F****** Sunglasses' are deliberately dumb eyewear — no cameras, no AI, no notifications — sold as a rebuke to Meta's smart glasses. Product design as a position statement about ambient AI capture.
items.title: Normal F****** Sunglasses are the perfect answer to Meta's creepy smart glasses

items.excerpt: Desktop CNC is getting cheap, quiet and software-friendly enough to follow the 3D printer's path into makers' spare rooms. If digital fabrication gets that accessible, subtractive making becomes a normal step in a designer's prototyping loop.
items.title: Forget 3D printers, CNC machines could be the next big craze of 2027

items.excerpt: Makera Studio pulls CAM, simulation, guided setup and mobile machine control into one environment for its Carvera desktop CNC line, plus a shared project library. It collapses the gap between a CAD file and a cut part for small design shops.
items.title: Makera links CNC software, mobile control and project sharing

items.excerpt: PTC's Codebeamer update adds semantic search over requirements plus variant management and deeper PLM integration. For hardware product teams it means the spec trail behind a design decision becomes queryable in natural language.
items.title: PTC updates Codebeamer, AI and Pure Variants ALM software

items.excerpt: XGIMI's MemoMind One passed $1M on Kickstarter with camera-less display glasses, betting that people want a heads-up screen without a face-mounted camera. The funding is a real signal about which smart-glasses form factor the public will actually wear.
items.title: 'MemoMind One' Kickstarter Hits $1M, Making a Strong Case for Camera-less Display Glasses

items.excerpt: Viture Pro 2 launches at $300 as the company's thinnest and lightest AR glasses, alongside a pocketable USB-C dock. The industrial-design race in display glasses is now being won on grams and comfort rather than feature lists.
items.title: Viture Pro 2 is the Company's Thinnest & Lightest AR Glasses Yet, Priced at $300

items.excerpt: Supernatural's head of fitness explains rebuilding the VR exercise app's experience design after leaving Meta — what coaching, pacing and embodiment have to feel like in headset. A rare candid look at designing for the body rather than the screen.
items.title: Supernatural's head of fitness on rebooting the VR exercise app after leaving Meta

items.excerpt: Before ethical principles can guide an AI product, they have to be translated into rules people can actually agree on and check. The piece pushes designers to turn vague value statements into operational constraints.
items.title: Defining ethical design for machines

items.excerpt: A argument for treating the AI-era app as a cybernetic system — feedback loops between user, model and interface — rather than a set of screens. It reframes what a designer is actually shaping when the product responds to itself.
items.title: The cybernetic application

items.excerpt: Wile E. Coyote's catalogue of ACME failures used as a design-practice case study: untested assumptions, no fallback states, and products that only work in the happy path. A funny frame for the failure modes AI-generated designs keep repeating.
items.title: Design @ ACME

items.excerpt: A walkthrough of free tools that convert your own handwriting into an installable font on Android, Windows or macOS. Type design as a personalisation move — and a low-effort counterweight to interfaces that all look machine-made.
items.title: Turn your handwriting into a font for Android, Windows, or MacOS

items.excerpt: Liquid AI released LFM2.5-2.6B, an open-weight model built for agentic workloads that runs on hardware as small as a Raspberry Pi — no cloud, no GPU. On-device agents put creative and client work inside the studio's own machines.
items.title: No cloud, no GPUs, no problem: Liquid AI's new model LFM2.5-2.6B brings powerful AI agents to devices everywhere

items.excerpt: A build guide for a fully local, real-time voice agent using Transformers.js and WebGPU — no server round trips, no third-party API, sub-second latency. Voice as an interface layer you can prototype without shipping user audio anywhere.
items.title: How to build a real time voice AI agent in the browser
